texts:
The avatar engine with the most realistic demo is usually one you cannot put in a product. Most of the highest-fidelity work in this field is research code under a non-commercial license.

The Avatar Engines Atlas maps 24 engines and puts each license next to the technique. Turn on the commercial-use filter and 5 remain.

three.ws/avatar-engines

Each card states what the engine takes in, what it outputs, what it runs on, and what its license permits.

For the photoreal engines a product could license, a training run per subject is not something you put behind a button.

2 of the 24 are live on the platform today: the MIT-licensed generator behind the free text and image to 3D lane, and the skeleton the animation pipeline canonicalizes against.

Filters are written into the URL, so a filtered view is a link you can share.

issues.problem: The 5.3s frame sits under the caption "Keep only licenses you can ship under" and shows the Commercial-use only checkbox engaged while the count still reads "24 of 24 engines". The run did wait for and see "5 of 24 engines", so the state exists; this frame appears to be transitional and slightly undercuts the caption it sits under.
issues.fix: If recutting the reel is cheap, shift this caption half a second later so it lands on the frame where the count has updated to 5 of 24; otherwise the run record confirms the state change is filmed and this is acceptable.

issues.quote: the skeleton the animation pipeline canonicalizes against
issues.problem: "Canonicalizes against" is precise but dense; a reader outside the animation-retargeting world may not parse why a skeleton is one of the two live engines.
issues.fix: Optional: "the Mixamo skeleton the three.ws animation pipeline retargets every rig to". Not required; the developer lane supports the current phrasing.
